Ca2+-ATPAse undergoes a major conformational change on going from the E1 state to the E2 state.
the c.d. spectrum of Ca2+-pump protein is not altered by the E1---- E2 transition.
the E1-E2 transition in the sarcoplasmic-reticulum Ca2+ pump occurs without significant changes in the secondary structure of the polypeptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the Ca2+-transport ATPase of sarcoplasmic membranes.
the structural basis of the E1---- E2 transition in Ca2+-ATpase in native SR, in FITC-labelled SR and in solubilizated SR.
the structural basis of the E1---- E2 transition in Ca2+-ATpase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the E1 and the E2 states of the ATPase in SR are structurally very similar.
the E1--E2 transition does not involve major changes in secondary structures.
the E1 and the E2 states are very similar with respect to secondary structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there are no major conformational changes in the polypeptide chain during the E1----2 transition in the SR Ca2+-ATpase, although it has been shown that there are changes in the conformation of the phosphoenzyme and in the binding site for ATP.
the Ca2+-binding sites are located in a region that is highly flexible, whereas the catalytic and the phosphorylation domains are more rigid.

the E1 state of Ca2+-translocating ATPase is characterized by a high affinity for Ca2+ ions, and a low affinity for vanadate ions, whereas the E2 state has a high affinity for vanadates, and a low one for Ca2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the c.d. spectrum of a protein is not always a good indicator of its conformation.

, in the E1---- E2 transition of Ca(2+)-ATPase, the secondary structures do not change significantly, which implies that the transition does not involve a significant change in the conformation of the protein backbone.
the Ca2+-transport ATPase in sarcoplastic reticulum is not a good model for the P-type ATPases in general.
